Benchmarking: cell type annotation

2026-08-10

Runs: pilot 260423_VH01624_453_222HWMYNX (HBDN206-MNpCT, HBDN392-AML-MDS, HBDN501-AML-KMT2A, MOLM13) and 260528_VH01624_464_222K7VKNX / LK2 (normal-01, HBDN376-TP53, HBDN498-TP53, APOP576-TP53).

Analysis finished: 2026-08-09 - the most recent of the 37 figures shown below.

Report generated: 2026-08-10 by 05.celltype_annotation_report.Rmd, from the outputs of steps 01-04 in this folder.

Cells are annotated by projecting them into the Zeng et al. bone marrow reference with Symphony, rather than by clustering and scoring marker genes. The reference carries its own mapping-error QC, so a cell can come back with no label at all. This report covers how the projection behaves on our data, how many cells it refuses, what those cells are, and how much the labels can be trusted.

For full report, download celltype_annotation_report.html in the attachment and open in a browser.

Code used - attached and in the github repository: https://github.com/nbartonicek/surface_proteome_dev/tree/main/lab_archives/7.Benchmarking-cell_type_annotation

Aim

Establish reference-based annotation as the project’s cell typing, and find out where it breaks:

  • how many cells does the reference refuse to label, and is that number stable between runs
  • what are the refused cells - real biology the reference does not contain, or bad cells
  • how much confidence sits behind the labels that do survive, and for which populations
  • fine versus broad labels: which one downstream analysis should key on

Conclusions

  • BoneMarrowMap projection works and is what the project uses. It annotates 92.05% of pilot cells and 94.52% of LK2 cells, at the default MAD_threshold of 2.5
  • the cells it refuses are bad cells, not unknown biology. They are half the depth of the cells that pass (837 vs 2556 genes in LK2), have higher mitochondrial and four times lower ribosomal content, and are enriched for HTO-negative droplets. Forced to pick a neighbour they land on late erythroid and monocyte, the two lowest-complexity populations
  • the rejection rate is a readout of how far a sample sits from normal marrow. In the pilot the normal donor loses 4.8% and the leukaemias 10-11%; in LK2 APOP576-TP53 loses 30% against 3-4% for the rest. A high reject rate is a flag to look at the sample, not at the reference
  • predict_CellTypes() does not re-label anything. The final label is identical to initial_CellType for 100% of cells; the only thing it does is set the QC-failed cells to NA. The NA cells and the mapping_error_QC == "Fail" cells are the same cells, 1:1
  • label confidence tracks how continuous the biology is, not how well the projection ran. Terminal populations - Monocyte, cDC, pDC, Plasma Cell, Late Erythroid - come back at a median vote fraction of 1.0. HSC MPP, LMPP, Early Lymphoid and Cycling Progenitor sit at 0.57-0.67, because the reference is resolving a gradient there rather than a boundary
  • downstream grouping must key on predicted_CellType_Broad, not on predicted_CellType. The fine column has 53 levels and only 9 of them appear in the broad vocabulary the lineage lists and the bespoke palette are written against. Keyed on the fine label, 84.3% of pilot cells and 89.1% of LK2 cells fall into “Other”; keyed on the broad label, none do
  • the Unknown cells sit with erythroid and pro-monocyte. On 02a_umap_native_unknown_highlighted.pdf the majority fall in the erythroid / late erythroid territory and in pro-monocyte, rather than scattering across the map
  • the pipeline and the standalone scripts disagree on the threshold. nextflow/bin/annotate.R runs at MAD_threshold = 4; steps 01 and 02 ran at the BoneMarrowMap default of 2.5. Going 2.5 -> 3 -> 4 roughly halves the rejection rate (pilot 7.95 -> 6.36 -> 3.91%, LK2 5.48 -> 3.58 -> 1.75%) without changing which samples are hardest to place. Given what section 3 shows the rejected cells to be, 2.5 is the better setting - but 4 is what production currently runs, and that should be settled on purpose
  • there is no confidence cutoff anywhere in the annotation. predict_CellTypes() reports the k = 30 vote share and never thresholds on it; the only gate is the mapping-error QC

1. The reference

The reference is BoneMarrowMap (Zeng et al.), a Symphony reference built on normal human bone marrow. It ships as a 345 MB reference object plus a 221 MB uwot model, both downloaded once into annotation/. Projection is map_Query() -> calculate_MappingError() -> predict_CellTypes() -> predict_Pseudotime(), with the demultiplexed sample as the batch variable so Symphony harmonises across donors within a pool rather than treating the GEM well as one batch.

00a_BoneMarrowMap_reference_broad_celltype.pdf

The reference itself, coloured by broad cell type in the project palette. Query cells are placed into this space; they do not move it. Stromal is the grey island - it is in the reference, and it is the population that used to be dropped from every figure by the palette bug described in section 9.

The reference returns two label columns, and the difference between them is the single thing most likely to cause trouble downstream:

4. How much the surviving labels can be trusted

There is only one cutoff in the whole annotation, and it is the mapping-error one. predict_CellTypes() calls knnPredict_Seurat() with k = 30: each query cell is given the majority label of its 30 nearest reference neighbours in harmonised PCA space. predicted_CellType_prob is the fraction of those 30 that voted for the winning label - so it is a vote share, not a posterior probability, and every value it can take is a multiple of 1/30. In LK2 it takes 25 distinct values, the lowest being 0.2 (6 of 30).

predict_CellTypes() then does exactly one thing with that number: nothing. It never thresholds on it. The only cell it sets to NA is the cell whose mapping_error_QC is Fail. So a label assigned on a 7-to-30 plurality is stored with the same standing as one assigned unanimously, and it is up to whoever reads the object to decide whether to trust it. Nothing downstream in this project currently filters on it either.

That makes the distribution below worth reading properly rather than skimming: it is the only description of how firm each label is.

Label confidence over cells that pass QC
run n prob_p05 prob_q25 prob_median prob_q75 percent_above_0.5 percent_above_0.8
LK1 pilot 19828 0.400 0.567 0.767 0.967 83.8 44.7
LK2 20605 0.433 0.633 0.900 1.000 88.5 57.4

03_label_confidence.pdf

One bar is one neighbour changing its vote. The dashed lines are reading aids, not thresholds the tool applies: 1/30 is the floor, 0.5 is where a label stops being a true majority and becomes a plurality, 1.0 is unanimous. 34% of LK2 labels are unanimous; 8% sit below the majority line and are the ones to be careful with.

04_label_confidence_by_celltype.pdf

Median confidence by broad cell type. The low end is HSC MPP, LMPP, Early Lymphoid, Cycling Progenitor and Early GMP; the high end is Monocyte, cDC, pDC, Plasma Cell and Late Erythroid.

This is not a quality gradient. The populations with low confidence are the ones that are genuinely continuous - a cell part way along the HSC-to-LMPP axis should not get a unanimous vote, and the fact that it does not is the reference behaving correctly. It does mean that any analysis that treats HSC MPP as a discrete population is working with a soft boundary, which is worth remembering for the biotin split and for the surfaceome comparisons.

5. What predict_CellTypes() actually does

initial_CellType versus predicted_CellType
run n n_initial_NA n_final_NA n_QC_fail final_NA_equals_QC_fail percent_label_unchanged
LK1 pilot 21541 0 1713 1713 TRUE 100
LK2 21800 0 1195 1195 TRUE 100

initial_CellType is never NA, predicted_CellType is NA for exactly the QC-failed cells, and wherever both are present they are identical for 100% of cells in both runs. So the second call is a gate, not a second opinion: it does not revise labels, it withholds them. That matters for anyone reading the object - initial_CellType is not a draft that got improved, it is the same answer without the QC applied.

Step 01 here is keyed on the broad column, and step 02 (the LK2 version that became the pipeline process) already was.

7. The mapping-error threshold

2.5 is the BoneMarrowMap default, and it is what the standalone scripts in steps 01 and 02 ran. The pipeline does not use it. nextflow/bin/annotate.R runs at MAD_threshold = 4; only nextflow/bin/lib_early_qc_annotation.R still has 2.5. So the figures in results/seurat_annotated/ are at 2.5 and anything coming out of results_nf/ is at 4, and the two are not interchangeable.

The score itself does not depend on the threshold - calculate_MappingError() stores mapping_error_score per cell and then calls Pass/Fail on score < median(score) + MAD_threshold * mad(score), with median and MAD taken over the whole object. So the sweep below is computed directly from the stored score rather than by re-projecting. Recomputing the 2.5 call reproduces the stored mapping_error_QC for 100% of cells in both runs, which is what makes the other two columns trustworthy.

06_MAD_threshold_sweep.pdf

Every sample moves in the same direction and keeps its rank - the threshold changes how much is cut, not which samples are hardest to place. APOP576-TP53 still loses 11.6% at 4, more than any other sample loses at 2.5.

Going from 2.5 to 4 roughly halves the rejection rate - 7.95% to 3.91% in the pilot, 5.48% to 1.75% in LK2 - and 3 sits between them. Since section 3 shows the rejected cells are shallow, ribosome-poor and enriched for HTO negatives, the cells recovered by relaxing the threshold are mostly ones there is no good reason to keep. That argues for 2.5 rather than the 4 the pipeline currently runs, but it has not been changed, so the discrepancy stands and is worth resolving deliberately rather than by drift.

9. What was run

Step Script What
00 00.celltype_palette.R The bespoke broad-cell-type palette, lineage vocabulary and the check_palette() guard, defined once and sourced by steps 01-03. Run directly, it redraws the reference UMAPs.
01 01.annotate_LK1_pilot.R BoneMarrowMap projection of the LK1 pilot, MAD 2.5.
02 02.annotate_LK2.R The same projection on LK2. This is the version that became the pipeline’s 08_annotate process.
03 03.check_unannotated_cells.R Re-projects the LK2 pipeline checkpoint at MAD 4 and characterises the cells that still fail - QC covariates, donor, HTO class, native cluster, nearest annotated neighbour.
04 04.annotation_benchmark_summary.R Scores the annotation from the metadata tables alone: reject rates, rejected-cell profile, label confidence, initial-versus-final label, fine-versus-broad vocabulary, the MAD threshold sweep.
04a 04a.projected_umaps.R Redraws the projected UMAP for both runs in the broad palette. Separate from step 04 because it is the only step that loads the ~450 MB projected objects.
05 05.celltype_annotation_report.Rmd This report.

Steps 01 and 02 are collated from backup/10.annotate.R, backup/10a.annotate.R, backup/10b.annotate_DSB.R and 8.annotate.R. 10.annotate.R is superseded - none of its output names survive in results/. 10a and 10b are the same script run twice with different ADT assays, which is now the step 01 argument. Three fixes went in on the way:

  • 10a had a marker_map / plot_df block sitting above the code that creates the objects it references, so it could only ever have been run interactively out of order. Removed.
  • 10a.heatmap_cell_type_all.pdf is 0 bytes on disk because scaling a zero-variance row gives NaN and pheatmap will not draw it. Fixed in both steps.
  • the numbat export loops at the tails of 10a and 8.annotate.R belong to the CNV work, not to annotation. Dropped from both.
  • every script carried its own copy of the palette, and the copies had drifted. All of them listed GMP - a label the reference never emits, since it splits that population into Early GMP and Late GMP - and none had an entry for Stromal, which the reference does emit. Because the plots do factor(CellType_Broad, levels = names(celltype_cols)), every stromal cell was being set to NA and dropped at the plotting step. That is why stromal cells looked unannotated: they were annotated, they were being discarded when drawn. The palette now lives in step 00 with Stromal in grey, and check_palette() raises a warning instead of silently dropping anything it does not recognise.

11. Caveats

  • steps 01 and 02 are the collated, cleaned versions of the scripts that produced the original annotation, and were not re-executed - the projections they wrote in May and June are what everything here is computed from. Steps 00, 03, 04 and 04a were run fresh, which is what Analysis finished reflects. Step 03 reused its saved annotated object rather than re-projecting, so only its figures are new, not its numbers
  • the pilot and LK2 numbers come from two different input objects and two different upstream CITE QC runs, so the difference in reject rate between runs is not a controlled comparison. The per-sample ordering within each run is, and so is the threshold sweep, which moves the same cells against the same score
  • step 03 runs on the pipeline checkpoint at MAD_threshold = 4, not on the step 02 object at 2.5. Its 1.35% Unknown and step 02’s 5.48% Fail are therefore both correct and not directly comparable - the sweep in section 7 is the like-for-like version, since it recomputes both thresholds against the same cells
  • the ADT/CITE marker projections that steps 01 and 02 also write are not shown here. The step 01 ADT_ASSAY argument still selects between ADT_CLR and CITE_DSB for them, and both were run; the figures are on disk under projectionFigures/
  • APOP576-TP53’s 30% reject rate has not been chased down beyond noting it. It is the sample to look at first if that number matters
  • pseudotime is inherited from the reference, not computed on our cells, so it should be read as “where in the normal trajectory does this cell project”, not as a trajectory of the leukaemia
